memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Follow‑up of migraine, anxiety and type 2 diabetes.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: He reports occasional throbbing frontal headaches relieved by sumatriptan, mild worry and restless sleep, and stable polyuria. No hypoglycaemic episodes.

EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 70 kg, height 1.68 m, BMI 24.8 (overweight). Pulse regular, fundoscopic view normal, neurological exam shows no focal deficit.

IMPRESSION: Migraine controlled on prophylactic propranolol; generalised anxiety disorder stable on escitalopram and buspirone; diabetes well controlled with metformin and glimepiride. Advised weight reduction as BMI is overweight.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue propranolol 40 mg OD, sumatriptan 50 mg SOS, topiramate 25 mg HS, naproxen 500 mg SOS; escitalopram 5 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD; metformin 500 mg BD, glimepiride 1 mg OD before breakfast. Review in 3 months. Return if new visual loss, severe headache with vomiting, chest pain, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Routine review with lipid screen and diabetes check.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: He notes headaches less frequent, anxiety unchanged, and occasional leg swelling after long walks.

EXAMINATION: BP 142/88 mmHg, weight 71 kg, BMI 25.2 (obese). Mild pitting edema ankles. Cardiovascular and respiratory exams normal.

IMPRESSION: Migraine improved; anxiety stable; diabetes control adequate but weight increased to obese range. Lipids show borderline LDL; fasting glucose normal. Reinforce diet and activity due to obesity.

ARRANGEMENTS: Increase metformin to 850 mg BD; continue glimepiride 1 mg OD, sitagliptin 100 mg OD, empagliflozin 10 mg OD. Keep migraine and anxiety meds unchanged. Order fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar today. Review in 3 months. Return if worsening edema, dyspnea, chest pain, or sudden vision change.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 5.2 mmol/L (ref <5.2), LDL 3.1 mmol/L (ref <2.6), HDL 1.2 mmol/L (ref >1.0), triglycerides 1.8 mmol/L (ref <1.7). Fasting blood glucose 98 mg/dL (ref 70‑100).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Autumn review; influenza vaccine offered.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: He reports a mild frontal headache yesterday relieved by sumatriptan, anxiety unchanged, and no urinary symptoms.

EXAMINATION: BP 140/86 mmHg, weight 70.5 kg, BMI 24.9 (overweight). No edema. Lung fields clear.

IMPRESSION: Migraine occasional; anxiety stable; diabetes controlled. BMI at upper limit of overweight; advise continued moderate activity.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Give influenza vaccine (inactivated) today, 2025-10-20. Review in 3 months. Return if new neurologic deficit, persistent headache >24 h, fever >39°C, or hypoglycaemia with sweating.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Referral to Neurology for evaluation of refractory migraine despite prophylactic propranolol and topiramate. Request EEG and migraine diary review.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Neurology review: EEG normal, migraine diary shows 4‑5 days/month headache. Recommended adding amitriptyline 10 mg HS and continuing current prophylaxis. No urgent intervention needed.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Winter check‑up; diabetes parameters reviewed.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: He notes increased thirst and nocturia twice nightly; headaches rare; anxiety mild.

EXAMINATION: BP 145/90 mmHg, weight 71 kg, BMI 25.3 (obese). Random capillary glucose 162 mg/dL.

IMPRESSION: Migraine well controlled; anxiety stable; diabetes shows hyperglycaemia suggesting need for tighter control. BMI obese; reinforce diet and activity.

ARRANGEMENTS: Add sitagliptin 100 mg OD (already on) and consider increasing empagliflozin; continue metformin 850 mg BD, glimepiride 1 mg OD. Order HbA1c and urine albumin‑creatinine ratio today. Review in 1 month. Return if polyuria worsens, weight loss, or chest pain.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been feeling more worried lately, especially about my finances, and I’m having trouble sleeping even though I take my escitalopram. The headaches are still rare.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Mid‑year review with renal screen.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: He reports occasional mild headache, anxiety improved after counseling, and no new urinary symptoms.

EXAMINATION: BP 138/82 mmHg, weight 70 kg, BMI 24.8 (overweight). No edema.

IMPRESSION: Migraine controlled; anxiety improved; diabetes stable with current regimen. Urine albumin‑creatinine ratio shows early microalbuminuria.

ARRANGEMENTS: Stop glimepiride 1 mg OD due to risk of hypoglycaemia with empagliflozin; continue metformin 850 mg BD, sitagliptin 100 mg OD, empagliflozin 10 mg OD. Keep migraine and anxiety meds unchanged. Review in 3 months. Return if symptomatic hypoglycaemia, persistent headache, or worsening edema.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Patient booked a follow‑up visit with Dr Priya Natarajan for 2026-10-08 at 10:30 am. Please confirm.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Autumn review; influenza vaccine administered.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: He states headaches are infrequent, anxiety well managed, and no urinary complaints.

EXAMINATION: BP 136/80 mmHg, weight 69.5 kg, BMI 24.6 (overweight). Lung clear.

IMPRESSION: Migraine controlled; anxiety stable; diabetes well controlled; BMI overweight, advise continued walking and reduced refined carbs.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue metformin 850 mg BD, sitagliptin 100 mg OD, empagliflozin 10 mg OD; propranolol 40 mg OD, sumatriptan 50 mg SOS, topiramate 25 mg HS, naproxen 500 mg SOS; escitalopram 5 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD. Give influenza vaccine (inactivated) today, 2026-10-08. Review in 4 months. Return if new visual loss, severe headache with vomiting, chest pain, or fever >39°C.
